settings.editor: I use a range of evidence-based therapies to support clients in their journey towards healing and personal growth. My approach incorporates schema therapy, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), and dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT). I aim to look beyond symptoms, asking holistic questions to understand your whole story and help you truly reclaim your life.

To enrich the therapeutic process, you may choose to integrate arts-based techniques into therapy. Body mapping is used to explore and express aspects of the self, enhancing treatment outcomes and supporting healing.
Trauma can deeply disrupt your sense of safety, leaving your mind and body stuck in a constant state of survival.
When we experience complex stress or trauma early in life, we often develop deep, rigid patterns of thinking and feeling—called 'schemas'—to help us cope.
When emotions feel overwhelmingly intense, it can be incredibly difficult to find your footing or navigate daily life.
Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) is a foundational, evidence-based approach that helps us look at the practical connections between our thoughts, feelings, and behaviours.

My trauma-informed practice recognises that complex stress lives in both the mind and the body. By moving beyond traditional talk therapy, we utilise embodied practices like body mapping—tracing an outline of the body to create a life-sized map representing aspects of your unique lived experiences—safely allowing your story to be visually shared and understood.

settings.editor: When we experience complex stress or trauma early in life, we often develop deep, rigid patterns of thinking and feeling—called 'schemas'—to help us cope. While these patterns protected us back then, they can leave us feeling stuck in repetitive loops of anxiety, self-doubt, or relationship difficulties as adults. Schema therapy goes beneath surface-level symptom management. Together, we work to identify these underlying patterns, understand their origins, and heal the root emotional wounds so you can break free from old cycles and build a healthier, more fulfilling life.

settings.editor: When emotions feel overwhelmingly intense, it can be incredibly difficult to find your footing or navigate daily life. Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT) is a practical, skills-based approach designed to help you regain your balance. The word 'dialectical' simply means balancing two opposite truths: accepting yourself exactly as you are right now, while actively working to change the patterns that cause you pain. Together, we focus on building practical tools for mindfulness, emotional regulation, and distress tolerance, empowering you to navigate life’s challenges safely and with greater confidence.

settings.editor: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) is a foundational, evidence-based approach that helps us look at the practical connections between our thoughts, feelings, and behaviours. While standard CBT is excellent for identifying immediate habits and learning day-to-day symptom management, I view it as an entry point rather than the final destination. In our sessions, we utilize these practical behavioural skills as a stable baseline, allowing us to safely step deeper into holistic frameworks—like schema therapy and body mapping—to resolve the underlying roots of complex trauma.

settings.editor:
A Body map is a life-sized outline of the body filled with symbols, colour and texture that creatively express emotions and physical sensations attached to memories. The map is a tool to communicate complex experiences and support healing and growth.

My practice operates from an embodiment framework. This means we recognise that prolonged stress, depression, anxiety, anger, grief, shame, problems with managing emotions, emotional pain and childhood trauma, are not just stored as thoughts in the mind—they are physically held and expressed within the body itself. The effects of this can manifest as a deep sense of physical numbness or dissociation from your body, an internal feeling of tension and anxiousness from being unsafe, or chronic anxiousness and depression. We can sometimes use food control as an objective way to manage overwhelming bodily sensations.

By focusing on embodiment through tools like body mapping, we don't just talk about the symptoms. We work safely and creatively to understand the story your body is holding, helping you to bridge the gap between mind and physical self and support evidence-based therapies that are the mainstay of treatment.
